newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Kantor urges Japan to meet insurance talks date.
newsitem.headline: Kantor urges Japan to meet insurance talks date.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor on Saturday urged Japan to meet a December 15 deadline on bilateral talks over insurance, a senior Japanese trade ministry official said.

"In order for the United States to keep trust in the Japanese insurance market, we need the best and concrete signal from Japan by the December 15th deadline," said the Japanese official after Kantor's talks with Japan's Trade Minister Shinji Sato.
The two ministers are in Manila to attend the ministerial meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

On Friday, U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher also singled out the insurance talks as the key trade issue between the two countries. Christopher's remarks came in talks with Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda, also held in Manila.

Japan's Finance Ministry is in charge of the negotiations over U.S. claims that parts of the lucrative Japanese insurance market were closed to U.S. firms. Both Ikeda and Sato said they would relay the U.S. view to Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka.

Kantor also repeated U.S. demands to open governmental talks over the film market and said Japan must adopt further deregulatory measures in the car market and approve more dealerships for U.S. carmakers, the Japanese official said.
Japan has refused to enter into bilateral talks over the film dispute and asked a World Trade Organisation panel to arbitrate, saying it was a row between rival firms, not a governmental issue.
Sato told Kantor the two countries must first study the film markets of both countries, repeating a statement he made on Thursday in talks with Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky.
On cars, Sato said last year's bilateral agreement on cars and car parts was proceeding smoothly and told Kantor the Japanese government would adopt further deregulatory measures.
